title: A cyclone reaches the coast
body: A weather bulletin of the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warns that a cyclone has formed over the warm waters of the Bay of Bengal and is moving towards a coastal district. Pressure readings on the weather map fall from 1008 mb far from the system to 998 mb, 996 mb and 994 mb closer to its centre. The district administration asks families in low-lying villages to move to a designated cyclone shelter and keep an emergency kit ready. When the cyclone crosses the coast, strong winds push a wall of seawater about 4 metres high onto the shore, flooding fields and ponds. Heavy rain makes a nearby river overflow, fallen trees block roads, and electricity is cut off for several days. Weeks later, farmers notice that crops in the fields flooded by seawater are growing poorly, while fields flooded only by river water recover sooner. Over the next two days the cyclone moves inland and gradually becomes weaker.
